Md Hedayet Hossain, Advocate-----For the Petitioner. 
Fahad Mahmood Khan, Advocate-----For the Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Iftekhar Uddin Ahmed ----- Petitioner
Vs
Artha Rin Adalat No. 2 and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
"Let a rule nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why continuation of proceeding of the Artha Execution (Money Decree) Case No. 87 of 2003 by the respondent No. 1, Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka in violation of the provision as contained in Article 182 of the Limitation Act and or in section 28(1) and (2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 arising out of Money Suit No. 74 of 1990 which was renumbered as Money Suit No. 28 of 1990 now pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 3. In the backdrop of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this writ petition has been filed on the ground that the first execution case as all as the second execution case being barred by limitation, the proceedings of the Money Decree Execution Case No. 87 of 2003 is unlawful and liable to be declared as such. 

 4. Respondent No.2, the Bank contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying the materials averments made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that the Execution Case No. 5 of 1995 was admittedly disposed on 23-9-2001 and the record of the said execution case was destroyed and, so, the petitioner raised the question that both the execution cases are 'barred by limitation on the basis of information slip dated 28-10-2010 only, that after disposal of the first execution case, the Bank filed the second execution case in time and, so, the execution proceeding is lawful; that the writ petition is unspecific, indefinite and thus, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 5. The petitioner filed a supplementary affidavit stating that the first execution case is barred by limitation under Article 182 of the Limitation Act and therefore, the second execution case is also barred by limitation. The second execution case having been filed after 12 years from the date of decree the same is also barred by limitation in view of the provision of section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code, in short ). 

 6. Mr Md Hedayet Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the judgment and decree was passed on 19-6-1991 and the first execution case was filed on 27-11-1995 and therefore, the first execution case was barred by limitation under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. He further submits that the first execution case was disallowed on 23-9-2001 and thereafter the second execution case was filed by, the Bank on 28-8-2003 and, as such, the second execution case having been filed beyond the period of 12 years is also barred by limitation in view of the provision of section 48 of the Code and so, the proceeding of the execution case is without lawful authority and the rule is thus, liable to be made absolute. 

 7. In reply, Mr Fahad Mahmood Khan, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 2, the Bank submits that the first execution case was filed within time with an application for condonation of delay but the record of the execution case was destroyed and, so, the Bank is unable to show that the petitioner for condo nation of delay was filed before the Adalat with the application for execution of decree. He, however concedes that the second execution case was filed beyond the period of 12 years but adds that in view of the provision of section 28 of the Ain, the second execution case was filed within the period of six years from the date of disposal of the first execution case and, so, the second execution case is not barred by limitation and, thus, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 10. Be that as it may, admittedly the judgment and decree was passed on 19-6-1991 and the second execution case was filed on 28-8-2003 (Annexure D to the writ petition). Therefore, it is evident that the second execution case has been filed beyond the period of 12 years. According to the provision of section 48 of the Code, there is no scope to entertain any application for execution of the decree if the application is presented after expiry of 12 years from the date of decree sought to be executed. Moreover, the Bank did not claim that the judgment debtor by fraud or force prevented execution of the decree within 12 years. Therefore, it is evident that the execution case not having been filed within 12 years is barred by limitation. 

 11. It is true that the second execution was filed on 28-8-2003 after the Ain came into operation. But according to section 28(3) (4) of the Ain, the second execution case is to be filed within one year from the date of disposal of the previous execution case, and or within 6 years from the date of filing of the first execution case. However, as the Ain came into operation on 1-5-2003 the provision of section 48 of the Code and not the Ain shall be applicable for counting the period of limitation. Moreover, the second execution case has not also been filed within one year from the date of disposal the previous execution case or within the period of 6 years from the date of filling of the first execution case or within 12 years from the date of the decree and so, the execution case cannot be said to have been filed within time. 

 13. In view of the discussions made in the forgoing paragraphs, it is evident that Money decree Execution Case No. 87 of 2003 having been filed beyond the period of limitation, the execution case is barred by limitation. Therefore, the proceeding of the execution case appears to be without lawful authority.
